body: [{"streamId":"01a0ddac-2215-743a-b4bd-6c5d2e6537bb","eventTypeName":"Hall9k.Domain.Features.Tasks.Events.TaskAdded","eventDataJson":"{\u0022Id\u0022:\u002201a0ddac-2215-743a-b4bd-6c5d2e6537bb\u0022,\u0022ProjectId\u0022:\u002201a00d41-5d9a-73cc-b648-af431f721a71\u0022,\u0022Objective\u0022:\u0022An invite secret is about 60 characters instead of 162 (base32 or base58 encoding, a 16-byte random tail, a short root-fingerprint prefix) and a second node that proves the same secret inside one sweep window is told the invite was spent by another node instead of waiting as \\u0027not joined yet\\u0027 forever\u0022,\u0022AcceptanceCriteria\u0022:[],\u0022Type\u0022:\u0022Feature\u0022,\u0022AgentContext\u0022:\u0022Brian, 2026-09-26 08:2x EDT, in the hall9k project window, after asking whether invite secrets are reusable, whether they are key pairs, and whether they can be shorter. Facts verified against main at a1237be0e. InviteSecret.Generate (src/Hall9k.Domain/Features/Invite/InviteSecret.cs) joins three dot-separated parts: the minting root fingerprint (64 hex), the invite id (32 hex, Guid N format), and 32 random bytes (64 hex), 162 characters in all; only the random tail is secret, the first two are lookup keys already public in the ledger paths owners/\\u003Croot\\u003E/invites/\\u003Cid\\u003E.yaml, and the ledger stores InviteSecret.Hash (SHA-256 of the whole string). The joiner proves possession with InviteSecret.ComputeProof, HMAC-SHA256 keyed by the secret over its own key fingerprint. Single use holds: ProjectJoinCommand reads the ledger record before writing and refuses a spent or expired invite by name; InviteSweepEngine vouches the first node whose proof matches and marks the invite spent in the same tick. The race: two nodes that both write a valid proof inside one sweep interval (20 s default) get one vouched and the other left with a proof no sweep will honor, and that node sees only \\u0027not joined yet\\u0027 with no reason. Brian\\u0027s ruling: fold both into one small draft. Shortening: hashing cannot shorten a secret the joiner must present, so shorten the encoding (base32 or base58 instead of hex), the entropy (16 random bytes, 128 bits, ample inside the 72-hour expiry), and the fingerprint part (a prefix long enough to be unambiguous, refusing on ambiguity at join), keeping the ledger\\u0027s stored hash shape and the HMAC proof unchanged; the join command must still accept the current 162-character shape for invites minted before the change until they expire. Race: the losing node needs a readable outcome (a ledger fact or a transport note it can show in h9k status and h9k project show) saying the invite was spent by another node, with the minting node\\u0027s own status naming that a second proof was seen and refused.
